label: Charlie Chaplin Runs As Independent
detail: The film comedian Charlie Chaplin appears on the ballot as an independent candidate for President.
assumption: Chaplin draws a modest protest and curiosity vote, mostly from urban and younger voters, taken from both major candidates and from non-voters. He is not constitutionally eligible, so the model treats the ballot line as a symbolic candidacy.
facts_text: Charlie Chaplin, the English-born film comedian, is listed on the ballot as an independent candidate for President.
His name is widely known through his motion pictures and through his appearances at Liberty Loan rallies in 1918.

candidate.name: Charlie Chaplin
candidate.descriptor: English-born motion picture comedian and producer, living in Los Angeles
positions: Took part in 1918 Liberty Loan drives in support of the war effort.
Has made no public statement on the League of Nations, prices or Prohibition.
Speaks for ordinary working people, as his films do.
candidate.eligibility_note: Chaplin was born in England and is not a natural-born citizen, so the Constitution bars him from the presidency.

research_questions: How many votes did celebrity or novelty candidates draw in early twentieth-century American elections?
Which voters cast protest ballots for independent or minor candidates in 1920, and from which major party did they come?
How did the film audience of 1920 divide by age, sex, region and class, and how likely were they to vote?
